mechaber/1:main: One who wishes to recite the berachos in 2 or 3 houses should first recite the berachos in his house and eat whatev- er he intends to eat and then recite birkas hamazon. After- wards he may recite the berachos in the other houses and they will drink the cup of kiddush and magid and eat the vegetables and matzah and he will not eat with them. He may then leave them to finish their meal and they will recite birkas hamazon for themselves and if they do not know how they should repeat each word after him. He may then go to another house and repeat this procedure. Afterwards he may return home, recite hallel and drink the fourth cup. If he wants to visit the other homes first, he should recite the berachos without eating or drinking and then return to his house to recite kiddush. He may also complete the seder at home and then go to the other houses to recite kiddush without eating or drinking with them.

machatzit-hashekel/1:_: (א) And he blesses, etc. — for this is not a passing mitzvah — meaning we hold as Rama in siman 168 that bread, since blessing follows it — Birkat Hamazon — even if he went elsewhere, if he ate there he may bless Birkat Hamazon there at the second eating place; nevertheless l'chatchila forbidden to uproot from his place to go elsewhere except for a passing mitzvah, as stated there.
magen-avraham/1:א: (א) And he blesses Birkat Hamazon. But without Birkat Hamazon it is forbidden to uproot, even if he wishes to eat there more — because this is not called a passing mitzvah, for he can go to another place for Birkat Hamazon (Avudraham) siman 478 and siman 479.
magen-avraham/1:ב: (ב) And that’s not eating. Dea has already eaten an epicoman in his house and wrote the column in the name of Rabbi Dafi if he wants not to eat an epicoman until he eats a second in another house, and he will return and blesses a name where he is not allowed to eat at this night in the P, but in a written book that he does not eat an epicoman, but once, and he says:
magen-avraham/1:ג: (ג) And he blesses for them Birkas Hamazon — but he is forbidden to bless Birkas Hamazon on their behalf even though it is obligatory to eat matzah — if so Birkas Hamazon is also obligatory and he can discharge others [as siman 467] — Birkas Hamazon is different, as written And you shall eat and be satisfied and bless — one who ate blesses [Avudraham]; see Tur siman 486.
magen-avraham/1:ד: (ד) And he does not eat, etc. — for it is forbidden to taste before kiddush, as written siman 472; and if he eats there he will need to bless Birkat Hamazon as well.
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (א) (a) Mayan Dobby and so on, because there is no one who knows the Temple and the West:
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (ב) (b) We would like to bless you and so on, and we would say everything in the West as an order and food that is decorated and swayed by the High Court
mishnah-berurah/1:ג: (ג) (c) And the blessing of the food is not to be removed from its place to another place and even to eat more:
mishnah-berurah/1:ד: (ד) And afterward he blesses — meaning he sanctifies for them and blesses for them also borei peri ha'gafen and blesses karpas for them and recites Haggadah before them and second cup blessing and motzi and eating matzah and maror blessings; and although for other blessings of enjoyment we hold one cannot bless for others unless he enjoys with them — unlike bread blessings of matzah and kiddush of the day which are obligatory, therefore he can discharge others even without enjoying; and karpas is also considered a mitzvah and he can discharge others.
mishnah-berurah/1:ו: (ו) And he did not eat, and so on, for he had eaten an epicoman, and he was not allowed to taste again A glass of D.D. and a lawyer in the letter:
mishnah-berurah/1:ז: (ז) And they bless Birkat Hamazon for themselves — but he is forbidden to bless Birkat Hamazon on their behalf, for in Birkat Hamazon one does not discharge another unless he ate and became obligated; also as written "and you shall eat and be satisfied and bless" — one who ate blesses.
mishnah-berurah/1:ח: (ח) It is written in the word, and they will follow it, and they will call it a word in the word, and the other responds with it, and the blessing of the apostate is not only taught Blessing:
mishnah-berurah/1:ט: (ט) And he does not eat, etc. — and it is forbidden to taste before kiddush, as written siman 471. And if he intends to fulfill also through the kiddush he says before them, he will need to eat a kezayit there and bless Birkat Hamazon as well.
mishnah-berurah/1:י: (י) (b) All will be done - even praise:
mishnah-berurah/1:כ: (כ) (a) And he shall not eat and drink, as is the same as the case
turei-zahav/1:א: (א) And afterward he blesses for each one. Although for blessings of enjoyment we hold one cannot bless for others unless he enjoys with them — unlike bread blessings of matzah and kiddush of the day which are obligatory, therefore he can discharge others even without enjoying; and karpas blessing is also a mitzvah and he can discharge others. Rosh wrote: since the enactment is for recognition for children it is like a mitzvah blessing; Maharshal challenged: we say in chapter Afikoman and since it is only for recognition it is not a mitzvah; this requires further study — not that Rosh meant it is truly a mitzvah, rather since the Sages enacted it for recognition there is obligation and it is not like blessings of enjoyment; and practical law: Shach in Yoreh De'ah 214 and Chayei Adam and I wrote in other Acharonim follow Shach there and Chayei Adam; and I saw other Acharonim reconcile Shach's words; see Kaf HaChayyim to Sefer Ketubot Even HaEzer siman 218.
turei-zahav/1:ב: (ב) And he blesses for them Birkas Hamazon — meaning he does not join with them for zimmun, for he did not eat with them.
turei-zahav/1:ג: (ג) He prompts word by word. And there is no taking the Name in vain here, for it is like a minor who recites Hallel and they answer after him what he says; and so too Tur in the name of Rosh. And one might say: behold Rosh holds in chapter 3 "they ate" that one who did not eat can discharge in Birkat Hamazon one who ate — because of partnership; and if so, why is prompting word by word needed here? This is not difficult — for Rosh wrote there that d'rabbanan he cannot discharge, but Semag wrote plainly one can discharge, implying even d'rabbanan; and on this Tur disagrees in siman 186. Tur wrote: what Rav Alfasi [wrote] "and he blesses for them Birkat Hamazon," etc., and Rav Amram wrote there is no enactment to discharge them — for if he blesses Birkat Hamazon for them, then he cannot drink at his home Birkat Hamazon — end of his words; and Beit Yosef explained: since he blesses Birkat Hamazon for them, therefore he must eat a kezayit with them — then he cannot drink again at his home Birkat Hamazon — meaning he cannot eat and drink again at his home, for it is forbidden to eat on Passover night two meals, lest it appear as eating two Pesach offerings; and Rav Amram deals with one who preceded doing the seder in other houses — and there is no place according to this in what he wrote "then he cannot drink at his home Birkat Hamazon." And for practical law Ra'avad holds there is no prohibition when eating twice and blessing for them — from the prohibition of eating appearing like two Pesach offerings; what does this matter to that? — for eating afikoman is in place of the Pesach offering, and he eats it only once; rather the prohibition is that he cannot drink the fourth cup on which he says Hallel, lest he add to the cups — since he blessed Birkat Hamazon a second time, behold there are four cups; and therefore Rav Amram said: since he will bless here on a cup, how will he drink at his home the cup of Birkat Hamazon that he blesses at his home — behold there would be four cups; and what will he do with Hallel, which belongs on the fourth cup? As explained — this is correct. And what Tur wrote afterward "and so Rav Kohen Tzedek," etc. — on the essence of the law he agrees with Ra'avad that there is no enactment to bless Birkat Hamazon twice, only he gives another reason — namely that it is forbidden to eat twice on the night; for since he blessed the first time, eating matzah was removed from him, and although he did not eat afikoman, the kezayit of matzah he already ate counts for his obligation, as above siman 477 in the name of Avi HaEzri and Ittur; if so, what helps him that he eat a second kezayit of matzah later for afikoman — he already fulfilled; but Ra'avad did not give this reason of Rav Kohen Tzedek — for since he intends at the time of the first Birkat Hamazon not to rely on the kezayit of matzah he ate at first, but to return and eat again — then he eats afikoman — as explained; therefore he gives the reason from the prohibition of drinking after four cups; and all this deals only with one who blesses Birkat Hamazon twice — for Ra'avad from his reason, for Rav Kohen Tzedek from his reason; but if he interrupts his eating and goes to another house and eats afikoman there and blesses Birkat Hamazon there, there is no prohibition at all, even for Rav Kohen Tzedek — for in this case it is certainly one eating, as written siman 484 and as written siman 479, as I wrote. Tur further wrote: possibly even Birkat Hamazon one can bless in order to discharge them, since it is obligatory, etc., like dipping vegetables — end; and Beit Yosef understood that Tur wrote this as an explanation of the Rif's words, and it is not so — rather this is his own view, at least unlike Rosh, Rav Kohen Tzedek, and Ra'avad, who found no enactment in this; and if so, why not say that the Rif also does not hold thus — for behold he wrote "and he blesses for them" — meaning "and not he"; their reason for not agreeing to this is as Beit Yosef in the name of Avudraham, who also disagrees with Tur from the Yerushalmi, who said: every mitzvah from which a person is exempt, he discharges the public with it — except Birkat Hamazon, as written "and you shall eat and be satisfied" — one who ate blesses; but Beit Yosef rejected this — for since it is obligatory on this night, it is like the motzi blessing discharging others on this night even though he does not enjoy; but it appears there is another reason that the Rif, Rosh, and other Geonim did not agree to this — for certainly there is a great difference between Birkat Hamazon and other blessings obligated on this night: one cannot say that he discharges another and blesses on his behalf, except for something that is preparation for a mitzvah — namely that the other will perform a mitzvah after this one performs the blessing belonging to it; therefore regarding motzi, eating matzah, and dipping vegetable — properly this one blesses and the other eats that eating of matzah; unlike Birkat Hamazon, which is not preparation for a mitzvah that one can say that through it this one will fulfill the mitzvah — for he already did what he did, only became obligated to the Holy One, blessed be He, to give praise and thanks for the past in what he already ate, and another cannot give praise on his behalf, since the other will not perform a mitzvah because of him afterward; and this matter is exactly like one who sees kings of Israel, who is obligated to bless — can one think that one who already blessed for his seeing, and another comes who does not know the blessing and also sees the king, would require the one who already blessed to bless a second time on his behalf? Certainly not; and no proof is needed to refute this — the same applies here exactly: since there is no fulfillment of a mitzvah for the one who is not expert after this expert blessed Birkat Hamazon, it is certainly a blessing in vain; and it appears that Tur himself was careful about this, for he wrote: since they enacted four cups and enacted one of them on Birkat Hamazon, it is obligatory like dipping vegetables — behold he enacted what I questioned when he said that here too there is fulfillment of a mitzvah after Birkat Hamazon — that he will drink the fourth cup; he did not say the reason that since he has an obligation to bless on what he ate, only that certainly there must afterward be an enactment of a mitzvah; but this is not a true enactment — for Birkat Hamazon has no obligation and connection to the cup he will drink afterward, only praise for eating that passed; only borei peri ha'gafen is relevant to what he will drink afterward, and by virtue of this the Sages relied on it that the third cup be adjacent to it for counting four cups; but Birkat Hamazon was not enacted for the cup — unlike motzi and vegetables, where the blessing comes for them; and this matter is clear in my opinion, and I wondered at our master Tur who did not delve into this — and it is accepted and reasonable.
